paper.title: MemQ: Integrating Q-Learning into Self-Evolving Memory Agents over Provenance DAGs
paper.central_claim: MemQ integrates multi-step Q-learning over provenance DAGs into self-evolving memory agents with frozen LLMs, improving held-out, runtime and cumulative task success by propagating delayed credit beyond directly retrieved memories; convergence is established in a fixed-DAG evaluation setting.

provenance.notes: Configured Sol route supplied by controller; no trusted runtime receipt available, no model probing performed.

sections_read: Appendices A–F including all method, theory, results, settings and limitations

claims.text: MemQ improves mean held-out/final-runtime/cumulative success by 2.53/4.23/2.13 percentage points over the highest-average baseline for each metric.
claims.setting: five interaction/code/agentic benchmarks; benchmark-specific frozen backbones
claims.baseline_control: No Memory, RAG, prompted Self-RAG, Mem0, MemP, MemRL; same backbone/splits, some initialization/retrieval settings differ
claims.selection_vs_test: best bank selected on accumulation split; Eval SR separate, runtime/CSR accumulation only
claims.result_denominator: Eval 56.17%; final 71.50%; CSR 78.88%; train/test counts LLAB350/150, LCB140/35, BFCL400/100, DSBench350/116 over30/8 challenges, Automation480/120
counterevidence: Small held-out sets and no universal contamination audit; some configuration asymmetry; Self-RAG is prompted adaptation.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported within-benchmark retained-bank gains, not universal transfer or reproduced gains.

claims.text: Bootstrapping and multi-depth provenance credit help memory learning.
claims.baseline_control: remove bootstrap+ancestor effects or ancestor propagation while keeping one-step bootstrap
claims.selection_vs_test: evaluation SR alongside runtime and cumulative metrics
claims.result_denominator: Full method highest point estimates on all nine benchmark/metric combinations
counterevidence: No randomized-parent or paired memory-on/off identification; exposure may reflect correlation and co-retrieval.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Supports algorithmic component utility, not individually causal credit.

claims.text: Structural TD(lambda) converges and preserves fixed point.
claims.setting: fixed finite provenance DAG, gamma<1, suitable steps, fixed terminal values, unclipped updates
claims.result_denominator: unique linear fixed point under stated conditions; online graph expansion/clipping outside proof
claims.allowed_conclusion: Restricted theorem, not general stability certification.

claims.text: MemQ reduces DSBench training token consumption against MemP/MemRL.
claims.baseline_control: same DSBench training workload; includes memory calls
claims.selection_vs_test: training compute, excludes test and embedding compute
claims.result_denominator: 313.03M vs373.35M MemP and352.38M MemRL tokens; 16.2%/11.2% lower
counterevidence: Graph traversal, evaluation, embeddings, sweep budget and wallclock not fully measured.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Scoped LLM-token saving, not full-lifecycle cost superiority.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported post-selection memory-bank gains on separate within-benchmark tasks, with component ablations and a fixed-DAG theorem; neither improver-level improvement nor causal per-entry attribution is established.
unresolved: Growing-graph stability and full lifecycle cost
assessment.scope: A: feedback updates persistent non-weight memory content, utility and provenance reused in later tasks.

G.reason: Concrete delayed-memory credit bottleneck and clear MemRL/TD lineage, but closest-neighbor novelty is author-characterized rather than independently checked.

M.reason: Explicit MDP, first-order residual, parent graph and trace rule produce distinguishable predictions; attribution remains approximate and fixed-graph theory is narrower than online deployment.

X.reason: Construction, initialization, retrieval, minibatch update, depth/pruning and frozen deployment are reconstructable; growing-store/drift/retirement are not covered.

E.measurement.reason: Eight benchmark families, standard success metrics and separate evaluation/runtime/CSR definitions; judge validity and repeated-instance CSR are not independently audited.

E.causality.reason: Matched backbone/split plus gamma/lambda and retrieval/initialization ablations support components; configuration asymmetry and absence of counterfactual provenance controls limit clean attribution.

E.holdout.reason: Memory banks selected using accumulation split and then reused on disjoint test tasks; explicit LLAB no-test-tuning policy; category transfer/near-duplicate audits remain limited.

E.statistics.reason: Sample SD and approximate average CIs, explicit three-seed cost runs; no demonstrated main-result significance and full cross-evolution uncertainty, component sweeps point-estimated.

E.cost.reason: Training token breakdown includes memory/judge calls and reports seeds; excludes evaluation/embeddings, graph maintenance and whole-search cost.
